correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed all derivations from [U,U]=[W,W]=0 and the independently labeled U tensor W brackets (a,b>=2 eliminate off-diagonal quotient blocks). The invariant-center action is S=A tensor I+I tensor B with arbitrary central shear. The idempotence equations T^2=T, S^2=S, S Phi+Phi T=Phi yield A,B projections and S^2-S=2 A tensor B; thus odd characteristic demands ij=0, while characteristic 2 has unrestricted i,j. The allowed Phi eigenspace blocks have dimension (a+b-i-j)s+(i+j)(ab-s), s=i(b-j)+(a-i)j, giving precisely the stated rank t+s and Gaussian-binomial multiplicities. For balanced n in odd characteristic, the log-q weight is (3n^2+2n)k-(2n+2)k^2 with maximizer ~3n/4. In characteristic 2, the A=B=I stratum alone has q^(2n^3) maps of rank 2n; all competitor exponents are separated by order n^2. Checked the actual verify.py construction of the Phi nullspace and source code; the explicit finite-field histograms are corroborative, not an asymptotic proof. A test of q=2,n=2 gives the formula 1+3072 z^3+74752 z^4+3072 z^5+512 z^6.

value.rationale: PASS: The number of distinct idempotent derivations of each operator rank is a natural invariant of a precisely specified graph Lie algebra, not a generating-set rank or arbitrary restriction. The stark fixed-field transition (typical rank quadratic in n in odd characteristic but linear in n in characteristic two) is mathematically structural and is not determined by the existence of gradings or Lie algebra dimension. The center shears are an essential, nontrivial part of the actual operators.
